**Finding submitted: deviation on § 7.7 (p0032), preferred position taken.**

- **Investigation:** § 7.7 was the only liquidated-damages clause in the document and it runs against us (15% of annual Fees per week after a ten-day payment delay) — a minor-breach trigger that compounds past remaining contract value, i.e. walk-away territory, well outside the fallback (single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees).
- **Cross-checks:** § 9.4 (accrued Fees only on convenience termination), § 2.1 (no minimum commitment/shortfall), § 8.2–8.3 (no renewal penalty), § 10 (refund of prepaid Fees), § 22.2 (audit shortfall = true-up, not a liquidated sum), § 27 (termination without penalty), § 21 (mutual cap) — no other Customer-payable liquidated amount. No service credits exist, so nothing running in our favour was touched.
- **Redline (validated ok:true, minimality passed):** replaced only the offending sentence with "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement or any Order Form.", preserving the 7.7 numbering; the fallback (three-month capped early-termination fee) is offered in the comment.
